plan_review.notes: Added surface-aware default resolution to preserve the lab/headless/CLI matrix; retained optional-purchase legacy precedence through the existing resolver; strengthened the hard gate with a pure registry-to-controls projection plus wiring assertions; required both lab and headless consumers to use one resolved featureFlags object; moved compatibility/default tests before migration. Scope remains AI-runner-specific.

findings.detail: In resolveAiFeatureFlags the `input[key] ?? definition.resolve?.(input) ?? defaultEnabled` chain is partially redundant for optionalPurchases: resolveOptionalPurchases already inspects input.optionalPurchases and always returns a non-undefined boolean, so the leading `input.optionalPurchases ??` term and the trailing defaultEnabled fallback can never both matter. Behavior is correct and consistent (default true either way); optionally simplify by documenting that resolve-owning flags bypass defaultEnabled to avoid future confusion.

independent_grade.notes: This is a clean, surgical centralization of the three AI-runner boolean gates into one typed registry. I verified the graded tree directly: typecheck:src passes and all 56 tests across the six changed test files pass. The registry's surface-aware defaults exactly reproduce prior behavior — lab defaults all true, headless floor1 settlement-routing true / floor2 false, weaponPersonas and optionalPurchases default true — and the CLI floor2 settlement-routing override is preserved via resolveHeadlessRunnerOptions. Backward compatibility is maintained: the lab reads legacy persisted aiConfig fields (including deprecated merchantWeaponPurchase/spellBrokerPurchase) through the resolver, and DEFAULT_CONFIG/mergedConfig no longer carry the removed flag fields (grep confirms no dangling mergedConfig.*/config.* references, and the Omit type keeps the compiler honest). CLI-omitted flags are correctly represented as undefined and dropped so the registry owns effective defaults, with tests asserting both omission and explicit opt-out forwarding. Scope is tight (ADR, ledger, registry, consumers, tests) with no unrelated refactors; layer boundaries hold (game/ai imports same-layer, lab is unrestricted); no determinism, Date.now, or Math.random concerns. The embedded review-ledger's independent_grade records a stale 'fail' about DEFAULT_CONFIG fallback values, but the graded tree already removed those values, so that concern is resolved. No criterion scores below 3 and no blocker/major findings, so the verdict is pass.
